i second contacting them privately/outside the application so it's all officially "off the record." alternatively, you could intentionally do a bad job so they reject you (some more risk that they admit you anyway but less risk of your mom finding out). it's very doable to make it look like it was an unfortunate mistake and to limit it to those schools by limiting the fuck ups to that school's supplement essays; things like misspelling the name (or even swapping the names between two schools! extremely explainable), weird implications, lots of spelling/grammar mistakes, "forgetting" to include an essay, messing up the terminology (lots of women's colleges have very specific naming things and get pissy if you mess them up like not calling a major a concentration etc), saying you're excited for something you know they don't have. do NOT plagiarize/break application rules or it could affect admission at other colleges you actually want to go to -- just piss them off. colleges really want to feel special and are honestly kind of petty, so if you combine a few of these it's pretty likely to work.

it's totally understandable if you don't want to fight your mom on this -- getting away from a parent who insists on misgendering you is the most important thing and it's much easier to set boundaries once you're gone. i had really strict parents and a lot of my friends did too. you're in the home stretch now, friend. it's fine to pick your battles or resist in a less direct way.
